## Shared vector emission — 2026-10-01

Raven now emits one-dimensional zero-based arrays of admitted primitives and owned
root classes through the shared logical type/instruction plan. Both target adapters
explicitly admit vectors; signature, local, field and property mappings preserve exact
element identity. Literal allocation (including empty literals), Int32 indexing, element
assignment and Length are supported. Evaluation is receiver/index/value order; aliases
retain the same array and contained objects. The unchanged Order declaration and its
three-element batch expression from the broad consumer execute in a separate array
consumer on .NET and binary neoCLR, in both source orders, returning 42.

Ordinary .NET remains the default and no Runtime Contract option is added. The native
adapter consumes the independent metadata API on codex/extended-cli-metadata (8e2a56ed);
compiler work remains on codex/metadata-consumer. CLI uses SZARRAY and standard typed
array instructions; the temporary native execution payload uses ArrayRef/newarr/ldelem/
stelem/ldlen. Length normalizes to Int32 explicitly, matching the source API. A later
native metadata backend replaces payload serialization, not this shared logical plan.
The host core is still the binding bootstrap; this does not implement general native
metadata imports or compile the complete collections application/System library.

Fixed-length type contracts, nested/multidimensional arrays, spread/comprehension expansion, covariance, imported
nominal elements, spans and element addresses remain outside this bounded shared path.
.NET keeps its general fallback. Array iteration is covered below. Backend primitive
type tokens are cached per output, and literals allocate directly without intermediate
collections; no performance measurement or speedup is claimed. C# shared-plan tests
cover Release/Debug execution and capability rejection; the executable ArrayChecks
probe verifies native binaries and storage projections in both source orders.

### Shared array iteration

Ordinary rank-one array `for` loops with an exact element local now lower into existing
bound locals, Length/index operations and branches, before either backend. Collection
evaluation occurs once. Nested loops, labeled continue/break, ordinary break/continue
and empty arrays retain their source semantics. Loops left for general .NET codegen
keep ownership of their unlabeled transfers, even inside a lowered vector loop.
There is no backend-specific language rewrite or additional metadata category.
Discard/converting iteration, generic enumerators and multidimensional arrays remain
outside this bounded native path; .NET uses its existing general path where needed.

Compared with the previous .NET generator-owned array loop, this shares lowering and
control flow across targets at the cost of temporary bound nodes and locals during
compilation. Runtime iteration remains indexed with no enumerator allocation. Performance
has not been benchmarked. C# tests independently validate .NET Release/Debug, target
admission, mixed enumerator/vector nesting and existing range/async/iterator loops
(39 tests passed). An additional fixed-length signature rejection check also passes;
this prevents silently erasing shape metadata. The expanded Order-array probe verifies and runs binary neoCLR
output and .NET output in both source orders (42), including side-effecting collection
calls and labeled continue. `array-runtime-validation.json` records source and runtime
SHA-256 identities. The full collections application and System build remain incomplete.

and bounds at the cost of retaining per-owner closure results. General base classes,

No Runtime Contract, emitter, bootstrap, guest API or encoding changes.

## Direct native compiler command (2026-10-03)

`rvnc neoclr --core-reference NeoCLR.CoreProbe.dll --reference Library.dll -o App.dll App.rvn`
now imports API-produced native assemblies using NeoClrMetadataReference and artifact-only
emission bindings. It selects CompilationOptions.NeoCLR and its explicit primitive/runtime
contracts. Native references never fall back to CLI projection. The core reference is
required when --reference is supplied; this is an experimental command compatibility change.
Without native references/core selection, the existing host primitive bootstrap remains
available. --system-symbols/--system-method is labelled legacy and remains an explicit
partial callable projection, not a native library import fallback.

Paired driver acceptance now uses `--dual-driver <rvnc.dll> <neoclr> <NeoCLR.CoreProbe.dll>
<fresh-output>`. Both .NET and NeoCLR Hello/helper and separate generic library consumers
execute (42); the consumer has no library source. Duplicate identities, missing transitive
dependencies, ordinary CLI references, malformed input and unsupported source reject without
publishing output. Host .NET runtime execution uses an explicitly hashed runtimeconfig.
The wider source-library/collections gate remains open; runtime encoding is unchanged.


Declaration-fact checkpoint (2026-10-03): metadata views now expose declared accessibility,
nominal abstract/sealed/static flags, instance/type-initializer classification, and
constructor enumeration on open/constructed owners. Constructor views share the callable
cache and substitute owner arguments. Raven maps supported metadata visibility to its own
accessibility and no longer decodes those type/method/field attribute bits itself.

This follows the existing CLI attribute contract rather than defining new access rules.
GetConstructors includes non-public instance constructors and type initializers explicitly;
GetMethods continues to exclude constructors. No invocation or implicit visibility filtering.
Existing canonical property accessor associations are retained. Supported native parameter
signatures remain by-value; byref/out, wider constrained/nested/value profiles still reject
at the reader boundary instead of losing their modes. This slice does not broaden encoding,
Runtime Contracts, the bootstrap, or runtime behavior.

External-interface gate baseline (2026-10-03): the paired harness now also supports
--dual-driver-external / --dual-driver-external-inventory with the same driver/runtime/core/
output arguments. Contracts, Box<T> implementation and consumer compile in separate

Required changes span SourceTypePlan/SourceInterfacePlan capability admission, symbol-only

### Native Self metadata contract slice (2026-10-03)

The host metadata API now retains `SignatureType.Self` and scoped `SelfTypeInfo` for
bodyless instance-interface declarations and associated properties. Runtime Contract
configuration is unchanged: Raven still needs its explicitly configured primitive core
and Self transport marker for the existing CLI bridge. No native Raven symbol or emitter
mapping is added by this slice. Native readers consume SelfType directly; reference-only
PE projection scopes the fieldless value-type marker to the supplied core identity.
Executable CLI emission rejects this native-only signature. This preserves contract
information without promising CLR execution of Self. Next adapt Raven symbols from
facade facts, then author native implementing-type substitution and typed calls from

explicit `--module` artifact; it requires an explicit `--system` seed. The path is
matched canonically to one supplied dependency, never selected implicitly from an
application declaration. The CLI derives the exact module/revision/type-row identity
from the already read artifact and passes it to the existing runtime load-context APIs.

serialized by assemble: use the explicit option again when loading the output. Metadata
seeds are decoded before linked validation so dependencies on the selected root can
resolve. The bundled seed is not automatically trimmed or substituted. Default loads
are unchanged. This is a deliberate host configuration beyond the ordinary CLR core
selection; it is useful for bootstrap experiments but requires an explicit compatible
seed and library catalog. No new metadata encoding or public library API is introduced.

semantic information. This documentation fix does not change runtime binaries or
claim to resolve the native reader's broader classification limitation.

### Source-library disposal ownership (2026-10-10)

The System.Runtime ownership manifest now explicitly selects disposal interface

owner and reject Iterator<T> conversions even though the source iterator implements
its own Disposable. This is the existing RuntimeDisposalContract, not a new opcode
or language spelling. Scoped constructor iterators lower to ordinary calls/branches;
normal scope exits dispose, terminal Faults do not unwind. Native metadata consumes
that same semantic plan. A library-native iterator remains a nominal interface;
there is no structural Dispose-name inference. Native for lowering still omits
cleanup in compiler b939cd696 and is the next compiler follow-up.

Submission rejects zero, foreign and expired identities before retaining work. Native

This does not serialize a scheduler, retain an invocation, route across heaps/threads,

### Runtime-owned registration lifecycle (2026-10-11)

The internal awaitable now uses SchedulerRegister(Int64 destination, fn<Void>) -> Int64,
SchedulerActivate(Int64 registration) -> Boolean and SchedulerCancel(Int64 registration)
-> Boolean, all exact reserved InternalCall declarations under the existing scheduler

Registration retains the callback in the current invocation; activation transfers it
to runnable dispatch, while cancellation releases only a dormant registration. Handles
are nonpersistent and invocation-owned. A dormant registration does not keep execution
alive and teardown abandons it. Cancellation of this handle does not alter Task state:
Task remains the operation abstraction and Promise its producer completion source.
The temporary 64-slot bound, integer token and unit callback do not define permanent
language semantics. Native metadata/codegen should eventually project registration
ownership for callbacks or saved activations without fixing these encodings.

Cross-invocation dispatch, concurrent transition semantics and automatic cleanup of
abandoned managed operations are still unqualified. The
[consumer](experiments/scheduler-continuations/README.md) retains all-mode execution
and native/interpreter lifecycle evidence; public Task/Promise registration is unchanged.

### Operation-wait proof of concept (2026-10-11)

neoCLR now experiments with source-local InternalCalls `RuntimeAsyncCreate() -> Int64`,
`RuntimeAsyncDelay(Int32) -> Int64`, `RuntimeAsyncComplete(Int64, Int32) -> Boolean`,
`RuntimeAsyncCancel(Int64) -> Boolean` and `RuntimeAsyncAwait(Int64) -> Int32`, all
under `neoCLR.Runtime` and classified as TaskDispatch. Raven emits ordinary calls;
no Runtime Contract option or automatic `await` mapping has been added. These are
private interpreter experiments, not public Task APIs or native ABI commitments.

The runtime owns an execution-context operation table and retained caller frames.
A pending wait returns to the host, releases managed graph access, and parks using
the durable scheduler wake latch plus a bounded cancellation/deadline timeout.
Queued callbacks may complete the operation, including after nested timer waits.
Completion/registration checks serialize on the same dispatcher, so this POC has
no cross-thread producer race. A future host completion ABI still needs atomic
publication and wakeup qualification. Handles are globally unique, context-local,
one-consumption tokens; they do not redefine Task's multiple-await contract.

Temporary limits: Int32 results, 64 unconsumed operations, LIFO retained chains,
no independent activation scheduling, no worker use, no legacy I/O callback pumping
inside the wait, and no JIT/AOT implementation. Cancellation faults the invocation;
unused operations are discarded on teardown. Native metadata/codegen must replace
the integer bridge with explicit operation/activation ownership, result rooting,
liveness and logical await links. Raven must use an explicit target capability
contract before mapping language await. Existing CLR AsyncHelpers lowering and
compiler-generated state machines remain unchanged.

The consumer instead passes the handle to a constructor. This gap is deferred for
an independently minimized compiler regression; it is not a language restriction.

### Pending self-await diagnostic (2026-10-11)

The private interpreter runtime-async POC now rejects a body's attempt to await its
own pending operation, including from ordinary helper calls. This applies to both
RuntimeAsyncAwait and RuntimeAsyncWaitCompletion. It raises a terminal RuntimeError
Fault at the offending call instead of parking forever. An independently dispatched
callback has its own activation boundary and may still await the submitting body.
A body may observe its own already-terminal cancellation through completion waiting.

This is a deliberate private POC diagnostic beyond .NET Task's general await
contract: it catches a provably unsatisfiable self-dependency before parking, at the
cost of a scan to the current activation boundary when establishing a runtime wait.
It is not general deadlock detection; indirect cycles and external missing producers
remain possible. No public Task guarantee, compiler lowering, Runtime Contract option,
metadata encoding or native/JIT capability changes. The author explicitly reaffirms
that Fault is non-recoverable: faults still end the invocation and are not stored as
recoverable task outcomes. Host cancellation and resource-limit faults remain terminal.

Validation: the regression previously required watchdog cancellation; 24 focused
runtime_async_await executable tests now pass, covering both wait forms, ordinary
helper attribution, terminal cancellation and independent callback waits. Existing

pass in that same suite. Compiler-native await/default switching and comparative
performance qualification remain open.

## Ad-hoc error union bridge (2026-10-13)

Author-directed scope: permit `Result<T, E1 | E2>` and `?` propagation of either
compatible error, without an inheritance/interface requirement or converters
written solely to aggregate errors. Named domain errors and nominal unions remain
preferable for many public APIs. This is a bounded integration task, not a change
to the platform roadmap's ongoing runtime-performance priority.

**Native intent:** structural union values retain an active value from the listed
types and expose the alternatives in the contract. The native structural metadata,
identity/normalization and backend operations remain future work.

**Temporary representation:** Raven's existing `A | B` binding resolves ordinary
`System.Union<A, B>` (arities two through five). The development System.Runtime
library now owns source-authored parenthesized nominal carriers. Native emission
uses ordinary generic nominal metadata, typed payload fields, constructors,
extractors and the union marker; it does not introduce a structural runtime type.
The documentation-only CLI reference projects those same declarations. Legacy
executable CLI importer admission is unchanged.

**Compiler ownership:** Raven main already executes the two-alternative error
propagation on .NET. Shared lowering now reduces newly synthesized residual union
conversions to carrier constructors. That general normalization is carried
separately to `codex/source-object-metadata-resolution`; no branch merge is needed.
Main commit `3abc0c954` and native commit `b6557ab85` retain the implementation.
The native branch also omits case companions for parenthesized unions: they have
existing type alternatives, not generated case declarations. Emitting a shared
empty companion for several arities previously produced conflicting metadata.
No Runtime Contract option is added; the existing explicit core/object/propagation
configuration and selected System.Runtime reference still govern native compilation.

**Costs and limits:** this follows Raven's .NET carrier semantics instead of adding
runtime type machinery for the immediate language use case. It retains a nominal,
ordered generic representation and an inactive default value, and callers may
expose low-level errors as API dependencies. It does not establish structural
normalization, arbitrary arity, union flattening or structural introspection.
No allocation or performance improvement is claimed. Native structural TypeSpec
and value operations must replace these carriers with a coordinated compiler,
metadata, verifier, interpreter/JIT/AOT and introspection migration; rebuild
consumers against matching artifacts when representation changes.

See [source, commands and validation](experiments/adhoc-error-unions/README.md),
[Union member reference](../api-docs/unions.md) and
[structural design proposal](proposals/runtime-unions-and-intersection-types.md).
The proposal remains exploratory; the bridge does not claim to implement it.

consumers pass, including wrappers returned with intersection contracts. Recursive
gates preserve ordinary readers, PE/CLI rejection and authored-storage restrictions.
Runtime Contract configuration and CLI carriers are unchanged. Task/async, open
parameters and native constraints remain pending.
[Profile and evidence](experiments/structural-compositions/README.md#wrapped-composition-metadata-and-raven-calls--2026-10-14).


### Intersection finality terminology — 2026-10-14

Intersection bounds exclude classes closed to subclassing (CLR sealed/final), not
Raven `sealed` hierarchies. Raven `IsClosed` and native `is_sealed` encode finality;
`IsSealedHierarchy`/`is_closed_hierarchy` encode the separate permitted-subtype
contract. Open and closed hierarchy roots and interfaces remain admissible; their
normal inheritance restrictions remain in force. Regression tests cover this
existing distinction. No Runtime Contract, CLI encoding or emission behavior changes.
The paired composition branches remain experimental; this does not enable the
feature on main or in published bundles.


### Host composition result locals — 2026-10-14

`MethodBuilder.DeclareExperimentalCompositionResultLocal(producer)` retains an
output-owned imported callable's exact result type in a native local, including
composition wrappers. Host wrapper consumers store/reload before forwarding; all
twelve paired consumers pass. Ordinary builder locals, CLI projection and Raven
source-local emission remain gated. Runtime Contract and bridge encoding do not
change; this is preparation for compiler storage support on the experimental branches.

The author clarified that structural types are fully introspectable runtime types
in the intended model, represented through signatures rather than separate nominal
declarations: tuples (later), unions, intersections and functions. Arrays retain
Array<T> backing. Present opt-in/storage/reflection restrictions are implementation
gaps rather than limits on the meaning of a structural type.


### Imported composition source locals — 2026-10-14

The experimental composition-call option now admits initialized Raven locals and
local copies whose exact type comes from an imported composition-producing function.
Portable lowering retains the producer symbol; the native adapter allocates the
local from its original metadata result descriptor, avoiding nominal normalization.
Flat unions/intersections, closed generic bounds and reference wrappers execute.
Unsafe union narrowing, default emission and PE projection still reject before output.
General authored structural storage, instance bodies and async state-machine fields
are not enabled by this slice. Runtime Contract settings and CLI encoding are unchanged.
This follows ordinary typed-local/definite-assignment semantics with a native structural
signature; it does not introduce a CLI carrier. Existing semantic type/hover identity
is reused, so syntax and TextMate grammar need no changes.

Validation: the paired runner passes fourteen interpreter consumers, including flat
and generic local/copy cases and both wrapper kinds. Wrapper fixture output identity
now matches its compilation, so its local check reaches the intended emission path.


### Cross-assembly Task composition transport — 2026-10-14

The experimental native reader now retains closed composition arguments on external
reference wrappers. Callable import resolves the wrapper against an explicit exact
snapshot catalog and validates its declaration; no ambient dependency loading occurs.
Raven supplies that catalog from registered metadata dependencies. Ordinary readers
and CLI projection remain closed. This extends the existing native signature model,
without a bridge carrier or Runtime Contract change.

The new Task probe compiles a nominal provider using the real System.Runtime
Task/Promise implementation, then constructs an experimental native signature fixture
for Task<Response | HttpError | JsonError>. A Raven source-local/copy consumer executes
and returns 42. The nominal control selects the library's Object and async identities
explicitly. An async Main binds its await and reaches the separate generated-field
storage boundary; this checkpoint does not claim await execution. Runtime calls and
state-machine field storage are the next slice. Existing host composition controls
and API snapshot checks pass. Website proposal status remains accurate.

Run `verify-task-await.py --raven <companion> --inputs <matching-native-bundle>` from
the structural-compositions experiment directory (or use its full path). Build the
runtime with experimental-compositions first. Validation records input hashes and
both source revisions; the development bundle is an explicit input, not a published
capability claim.


### Raven composition await delivery — 2026-10-14

The experimental compiler now retains an imported composition contract through source
locals, constructed Task calls and heap async-state-machine fields. Storage is enabled
only from exact output-owned imported result signatures; a semantic symbol cannot
invent a new native composition or silently replace a different raw descriptor after
nominal normalization. The option also applies to synthesized declaration/body plans.
Default compilation and CLI projection remain rejected without publishing output.
Reader gating now inspects fields and owned methods as well as free functions.

The host's explicit EnableExperimentalCompositionStorage(producer) registers the closed
reference compositions in that imported result. Registered descriptors can be used for
instance fields of reference classes, locals, native signatures and generic substitution.
Value-type/static composition fields, compound managed-reference parameters and arbitrary
unregistered composition authoring remain rejected. The experimental native reader
round-trips reference-class fields and nongeneric owned signatures; unresolved external
intersection bounds still reject because finality cannot be established by that reader.

The runtime admits direct composition fields on reference classes and nongeneric managed
reference-class methods/constructors. It reuses existing typed stores, object tracing and
heap async lowering, as ordinary nominal Task<T> does. Compound field addresses reject
both in verification and unchecked execution. No scheduler, Task implementation, boxing
carrier, metadata schema or CLI bridge encoding is introduced. This extends the earlier
research-backed native signature design; unlike CLR metadata, the field/argument type
can retain a structural union directly. The cost is an experimental compiler/metadata/
runtime contract that portable CLI tools cannot consume.

The real Task provider is built from nominal Raven code and transformed into a native
composition-signature fixture. Consumers are compiled directly from Raven using inferred
locals and await; no post-emission consumer rewriting occurs. Tests cover completed and
queued pending delivery of Response, HttpError and JsonError. Each keeps its result alive
across a second pending await, then verifies the concrete alternative. Error alternatives
are successful Task payloads, not Task faults. Source-authored structural Task return
syntax, full open generic composition support, guest reflection and JIT/AOT remain outside
this checkpoint. Runtime Contract selection explicitly names System.Runtime for Object
and async ownership; no defaults or published bundles change.

Normalized nominal symbols that no longer uniquely retain the raw composition are
rejected for synthesized storage; their existing exact-descriptor call transport
remains available. This avoids treating normalization as permission to erase bounds.


Validation for the await slice: all seven Task transport/delivery programs return 42;
all six await programs reject null payloads and verify the expected concrete alternative.
All fourteen earlier POC consumers remain byte-identical after final recompilation, so
their executable evidence is reused. Thirty-six composition runtime tests, ten Task
controls, three default-off checks, the host composition-import checks, twenty-seven
async-lowering tests and the API documentation snapshot check pass. The runner records

A separate .NET control, PortableDefaultReceiverTests.ReadOnlyFieldReceiverUsesDefensiveCopy,

Its general readonly-receiver behavior is deferred for independent reproduction/fix on
Raven main and deliberate carry-forward, outside this structural-type experiment.
No website build was needed; published capability status remains unchanged.

Nominal callers must obtain the nominal view and use that helper; Option/Result
declarations and their cases are not structural unions. Other nominal-helper
reorganization remains separate work.

The existing TypeShape runtime service keeps nominal marker slot 10 and adds

composition handle creation remains gated independently of the predicate semantics.

The aggregate CLI assembly is only the temporary compiler/documentation reference.

## Resolved external intersection bounds — 2026-10-14 development

Native method intersection bounds now admit imported closed reference types after

`AssemblyDefinition.ReadNativeAssembly(image, allowExperimentalCompositions,
IAssemblyResolver? resolver)` resolves each external intersection operand against an
explicit exact-identity assembly snapshot. It checks the named definition, enclosing
scope and generic arity, rejects final/value definitions, and caches resolved
snapshots for the duration of the read. The two existing overloads remain available;
without a resolver, external intersections fail closed. Default composition opt-in
and native runtime verification are still required. Bodies remain opaque; this API
does not load executable assemblies or infer interface implementation from members.

Raven's experimental catalog snapshots only the selected paths, then retries
unresolved images as selected dependency snapshots become available. Returned

cycles do not acquire a new resolver requirement. No adjacent assembly search occurs.
The explicit native composition capability now admits closed conjunctive interface
constructions in method bounds. Only intersection operands request definition-backed
admission; ordinary .NET and nominal emission remain unchanged.

and nested generic/Self substitution. That initial metadata-only slice rejected
executable structural tuples; the follow-up below adds opt-in interpreter values.

mappings; ordinary .NET ValueTuple behavior and Runtime Contract configuration are
unchanged. No temporary CLI encoding is introduced. The native replacement requires
runtime storage and positional operations, TupleTypeInfo, host authoring/import and
carrier-independent compiler lowering before removing nominal neoCLR declarations.
The runtime owns the signature/value work; Raven owns binding/lowering and import.
Focused Rust structural-tuple tests cover the metadata stage; existing source tuple
consumers remain the evidence for the still-nominal executable path.

The next runtime slice admits closed structural tuple values only with the explicit
`experimental-tuples` Cargo feature. Native aggregate construction and positional
field operations use synthesized ItemN members and existing value storage, preserving

runtime and JIT/AOT paths reject these signatures. Runtime Contract settings and
Raven source emission remain unchanged; compiler wiring must follow native host
signature authoring/import and tuple introspection. This is not a CLI bridge encoding.

queries the retained signature descriptor, not its name-free resolved identity.
Consequently equal tuple types can report different names; nested descriptors keep
their own names. Snapshots are independent. Identity-only reconstructed handles
report positional defaults. Unlike .NET TupleElementNamesAttribute, these names
live directly in native signature metadata; the cost is carrying descriptive data
separately from canonical type identity. The effective-name guest API intentionally
does not distinguish an explicit ItemN from its default; host APIs retain that detail.

This requires `experimental-tuples` and matching rebuilt source libraries. It adds
no Runtime Contract flag or CLI encoding; ordinary .NET output is unchanged. The
native TypeTupleNames runtime service backs the source provider. CLI reference
bindings exist only for compiler/documentation bootstrap. The guest fixture tests
two equal renamed native tokens, nested names, unnamed defaults and 180 repeated
queries per signature. The fixture isolates reflection from source tuple lowering.

Validation uses `target/tuple-names-libraries-v2` built with compiler
`793219d855b17f01fb805e215968b78871eb3804`, the existing explicit primitive bootstrap,
and the structural runtime branch. See
[guest name evidence](experiments/structural-tuples/name-info-results.json).
Tuple mutation, carrier-independent Raven symbols and project/catalog opt-in remain
separate follow-ups.

### Native local tuple mutation — 2026-10-14

With `AllowExperimentalTuples`, assignments to named or positional elements of a
local tuple now lower to native updated-copy stores. Nested paths rebuild each
containing tuple and write back the root local; earlier copies remain unchanged.
The RHS is evaluated once before reading the root for reconstruction, preserving
any RHS changes to sibling elements. Ordinary .NET emission is unchanged. This
uses native Tuple signatures and StoreTupleElement, with no CLI carrier encoding.

The bounded profile accepts local-rooted paths. Parameter/field/property/array-rooted
mutation, managed element addresses and open elements remain unsupported and fail
before publishing output. Binder mutability rules still apply. Runtime Contract
settings are unchanged; the existing explicit experimental emitter gate is required.

Validation: `NeoClrMetadataProbe --source-tuples` covers direct and nested writes,
named/positional reads, preserved copies and unsupported parameter mutation. The
TupleMutation consumer returns 42 in the interpreter with `tuple-names-libraries-v2`
(compiler `793219d855b17f01fb805e215968b78871eb3804`). The pre-change source tuple probe
passes; focused .NET tuple semantic/emission checks guard the ordinary target.

### Native tuple binding without nominal carriers — 2026-10-14

The explicit neoCLR Runtime Contract now offers
`MetadataImportOptions.UseStructuralTuples` (default false) and immutable
`WithStructuralTuples(bool enabled = true)`. With this option, tuple syntax and
native tuple imports produce structural symbols directly; they never look up or
construct System.Tuple. Native tuple emission now requires both this binding option
and `NeoClrEmitOptions.AllowExperimentalTuples`. Existing experimental hosts must
add `WithStructuralTuples()` to their metadata import options. Non-neoCLR targets
reject this option; CLI emission rejects the structural profile before output.
There is no project/catalog switch yet. Ordinary .NET and the legacy CLI bridge
keep their existing nominal tuple representation.

The native symbol has TypeKind.Tuple, no UnderlyingTupleType, assembly ownership,
metadata declaration name, constructors, inherited nominal members or interfaces.
Ordered TupleElements carry native names; ItemN aliases remain available for source
access. TypeArguments is empty: elements are not generic carrier arguments. Tuple
identity/hash uses ordered recursive element types, ignores names, and remains
distinct from nominal tuples. Substitution preserves the native shape and names.
Semantic lookup/display uses these fields directly; no syntax or TextMate change
is needed. This is the semantic counterpart of the existing native signature API,
not a new CLI transport.

Compared with .NET ValueTuple, the benefit is no arity-specific declaration or
attribute-name dependency. The cost is a dedicated structural symbol and explicit
identity/substitution handling. Native mutation requires a mutable local root;
immutable let roots and nonlocal roots reject before output. A general review of
value-type field writes through immutable bindings belongs on Raven main; this
slice enforces the native writeback boundary without changing .NET policy.

Validation covers carrier-free factory construction with no references, positional
identity/hash (including nested/repeated types), type-parameter substitution, member
names/display, target rejection, CLI rejection, source/import symbols, and separate
interpreter consumers. A nine-element tuple executes and mutates without any
System.Tuple`9 declaration; it returns 42. Nested mutation/copy and imported tuple
consumers also return 42 using `tuple-names-libraries-v2`. Focused ordinary .NET
tuple tests retain the existing carrier behavior.

This removes Raven's nominal backing dependency for the native structural profile.
It does not delete the old tuple declarations from the runtime library or CLI
bootstrap: those remain for existing bridge consumers pending bundle migration.
Open-element emission, nonlocal mutation, managed element addresses and broader
backend support remain separate work.

[Carrier-free symbol validation](experiments/structural-tuples/symbol-results.json) records the focused tests and executable consumers.

### Value and reference union alternatives — 2026-10-15 development

The author explicitly requires unions to support value and reference alternatives;
reference-only admission was a POC limitation, not the language contract.
Intersections retain their explicit nominal interface/extendable-reference rules.
The Web build's HttpError and JsonError declarations are nominal **value** unions,
so a conversion-only fix would not suffice. The source compiler has not been
relaxed to accept values it cannot yet emit.

The first runtime slice admits closed nominal records and scalar value alternatives
in structural unions. Explicit `box` followed by checked `castclass union<...>`
retains the native union signature and payload identity; `unbox.any` checks the
exact value type and returns a copy. Reference alternatives keep their existing
reference behavior. Direct unboxed stores remain invalid. Mixed union constraints
recognize exact scalar alternatives; whole-union coverage remains required.
Value types remain invalid intersection operands.

This is an interpreter representation choice, not a nominal Union declaration or
a new inheritance relationship. It reuses existing heap/GC/boxing support. Like
[CLR boxing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/programming-guide/types/boxing-and-unboxing),
boxing copies a value into heap storage and unboxing copies it out. The benefit
is reuse of checked payload identity and GC traversal; the cost is allocation and
unboxing, so this is not a claim of an optimal layout. Inline tagged storage is a
possible future backend choice, with copy/identity semantics to preserve.

This slice does not complete Raven authoring/import/conversion, generic value
wrappers such as Result, intrinsic String/array/function alternatives, tuple
alternatives, open types or JIT/AOT. It retains the current reference-container
null/default behavior; a general union default-value policy remains to be settled.
The fresh System.Web bundle remains blocked until compiler/host and generic
value-wrapper integration are completed.

Formatting remains a separate design question. The author proposed duck-typed
ToString because a union has no nominal declaration for an override. The assistant
proposed dispatching to the actual payload's ordinary ToString as the default;
no formatting rule or duck-typing feature is implemented by this slice.

Validation: `cargo test --test structural_compositions --test composition_constraints`
passes 41 composition and five constraint tests with the default feature profile.
The three new runtime tests cover mixed alternatives, copy-preserving extraction,
wrong boxed membership, explicit boxing requirements and invalid value intersections.
Existing constraint tests now cover scalar alternatives and reject incomplete unions.

## Value union source integration — 2026-10-15 development

Structural unions are value types regardless of their alternatives, with no nominal
base type. Guest reflection and Raven symbols now report that classification.
The native metadata host admits closed scalar and nominal value alternatives,
including imported values, alongside reference alternatives. Intersections retain
nominal reference/interface operands and explicit interface conformance.

Raven native conversion lowering boxes exact value alternatives and explicitly
unboxes on extraction. Reference alternatives preserve their references. Pattern
lowering distinguishes semantic value classification from the current interpreter
payload storage. Native projects use their existing structural composition
capability; ordinary CLI encoding is unchanged and has no structural carrier.
The runtime owns payload storage, the metadata host owns signature validation,
and the compiler owns conversion and pattern lowering.

This boxed interpreter representation is provisional. It incurs allocation for
value payloads and does not define the future native ABI. Inline tagged storage,
GC scanning, copy costs and specialization require measurement and design. A
method does not require a body per active alternative; generic specialization can
depend on the complete instantiated type, not merely its size.

`TryGetResidual(out HttpError | JsonError)`. Generic value-wrapper/byref integration,

## Range endpoint migration (2026-10-15)

The general Raven change defines `..` as end-exclusive and `..=` as end-inclusive

On ordinary .NET, stored/sliced ranges retain the System.Range ABI. Inclusive
System.Index ends are validated and converted with checked arithmetic to equivalent
exclusive boundaries: `n + 1` or `^(n - 1)`. Source inclusion spelling is lost in the
stored System.Range; selection is preserved. This general .NET lowering is not proof
of native backend support. Raven owns syntax/binding/emission; neoCLR owns its library
and native backend behavior. No new Runtime Contract option, structural metadata
encoding or native opcode is introduced by this migration.

sequence prefixes use OperatorToken for `..`/`...`; spread nodes use DotDotDotToken.

## Function-kind constraint direction (2026-10-16; feature branch)

The author requests `Signal<T> where T: func` for a library-owned function list
with event-like subscriptions, without special event metadata. On neoCLR the
constraint admits only structural function types, not nominal delegates or
objects declaring `Invoke`. The concrete signature remains reified. A generic
body with only this constraint has no known parameter/result signature to call.

The author has postponed invocation decisions: `Emit`, dynamic invocation,
multicast semantics, subscription policies and result/fault aggregation are not
part of this slice. A typed visitor was discussed as an alternative, not selected
as a public API. No reflection invocation bridge is introduced.

Native groundwork lives on `codex/function-kind-constraint` in neoCLR. Native
metadata uses the distinct `FunctionType` generic constraint; host SDK
`TypeParameterConstraints.FunctionType` retains it through snapshots/introspection.
This has no CLR GenericParam flag equivalent. CLI projection/export rejects it;
no System.Delegate substitution or loss of the constraint is permitted. Runtime
Contract settings and the existing function invocation ABI are unchanged.

Raven `func` syntax is not enabled yet. Investigation found that current function
syntax can use nominal Func/Action transport symbols. An attempted global switch
to structural symbols broke existing RuntimeAwait/RuntimeGenerator bridge binding;
the prototype was not integrated. The compiler must preserve the distinction
through binding, inference and native imports before this spelling is admitted.
Raven main and codex/neoclr remain unchanged; this note is on the feature branch.

.NET's System.Delegate constraint is the comparison point, not an equivalent
encoding: https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/csharp/programming-guide/generics/constraints-on-type-parameters
It constrains nominal delegate ancestry, whereas this native category constrains
a structural signature. This narrower semantics is explicit author direction.
The additional cost is a native constraint kind and compiler/import support;
there is no per-invocation dynamic checking implied by the constraint.


**Subsequent author proposal (2026-10-16):** provide a reflection helper analogous
to the array helper, conceptually `Reflection.InvokeFunction(functionObj, args)`.
The assistant agrees this is a plausible explicit dynamic boundary. The function
value retains its signature and bound receiver/closure; dispatch must use that
value, not substitute a bare method descriptor. A future helper must define the
argument/result value carrier, count/type and ref/out validation, fault behavior,
and AOT-compatible dispatch adapters. This does not require event metadata or a
nominal function superclass. The exact API and invocation semantics remain
unimplemented and deferred; this proposal does not implicitly approve them.

**Target boundary and later observer direction (author clarification, 2026-10-16):**
ordinary Raven/.NET behavior remains the default. Native structural function

profile admits Byte/Int32 pointer access with null/alignment faults, but cannot
validate foreign bounds, initialization or lifetime. Invalid non-null native addresses
can terminate the process. Native Slice borrowing, pinning and managed AOT remain
open. The Raven consumer reads/writes a C-owned allocation and observes the update
through C before release; low-level tests cover both typed and indirect instructions.

The matching metadata SDK now admits exact typed pointers for existing LoadObject/
StoreObject operations, retaining local/byref/out assignment checks and rejecting
mismatched pointees. Both the repaired compiler and SDK are required; an older SDK
rejects the emitted object operation before an assembly is produced. This changes
validation admission only, not the temporary CLI representation or native encoding.

The probe's CLI does not yet accept Raven seed/core verification inputs, so Raven

Dependency bodies remain verification-only. No compiler, Runtime Contract or metadata

No compiler, Runtime Contract or encoding changes. The separate direct pointer
read/write consumer remains JIT/AOT-qualified: interpreter dereference of untracked

## Public layout attributes and generated Raven imports — 2026-10-22

Raven now exposes LayoutKind, StructLayoutAttribute and FieldOffsetAttribute in
System.Runtime.InteropServices. MarshalAsAttribute accepts instance fields of value
types; the native emitter preserves their annotations instead of treating them as
misplaced import declarations. Sequential packing, explicit offsets/overlap, minimum
size and Boolean Bool8/Bool32 field representations reach the native layout decoder.
The attribute API records values; unsupported layout/marshalling is rejected before
native output. Managed object storage is not automatically converted or pinned.
This is the native-storage subset of the .NET attribute model, not aggregate-by-value
ABI support, class marshalling or parameter/result MarshalAs parity across engines.

A general parser bug was fixed on Raven main as 2073ee766 and carried deliberately
to codex/neoclr: following field attributes no longer parse as array suffixes on the
previous type. Valid multiline array ranks remain supported. Forty-nine focused
parser tests pass on main and fifty on the native target line. No new Runtime Contract setting
or bridge encoding is required; attributes retain ordinary source identities and
field-targeted native metadata. The native emitter capability change is target-only.

The native-library command optionally emits `--raven-imports Imports.rvn` together
with `--import-library <loader-name-or-path>`. Numbered NativeExport0/1/... declarations
bind exact native symbols. Struct declarations use explicit checked native offsets
and physical field widths; Bool8 storage becomes byte, not an implicit managed
Boolean conversion. The file is binding source, not a native runtime sidecar. The
object, C header and Raven file are created without replacing existing files; a
later output failure removes only files created by the current invocation.

Validation: all 23 native import/export integration tests and 19 focused native unit
tests pass. Source fixtures cover packed Boolean storage, explicit overlapping
fields/minimum size, Auto/invalid Pack/missing FieldOffset/incompatible MarshalAs
rejection, C11/C++17 callers and generated-import interpreter calls back into the
AOT library. All supported pack values produce C/C++ headers without unsupported
packing pragmas. Built-in Rust integration tests are used because the scalar backend
cannot execute the managed Raven test runner. Generated struct imports are not yet
qualified through the ordinary managed JIT/AOT executable pipeline.

The scalar JIT/AOT entry paths now resolve source layout attributes from the same
explicit runtime load context used by native-library emission. They verify the

I32 storage without changing native marshalling defaults. Raven emission and the

backend is not enabled by this scalar-profile repair. See the

## Nested platform record cases (development, 2026-10-23)

Environment discovery uses a static class and native nested cases such as
OperatingSystem.Linux and Architecture.Arm64. Ordinary .NET nesting, record equality,
virtual display and exhaustive closed-family matching are the semantic model.
Native emission now walks nested record declarations and admits a nongeneric case
whose direct base is its enclosing closed family, using the existing nested-type,
local-inheritance and positional-reference-record capabilities. No Runtime Contract
option was added. Other nested inheritance shapes remain outside this bounded
extension; explicit permits referring to nested types currently bind too early,
so these declarations use standard same-file sealed-family inference.

The metadata SDK retains the declaring type and direct base separately. Imported
case references retain inherited class slots and nongeneric interface implementations.
The native loader validates actual dependency relationships; reference declarations
are not authority to bypass them. The temporary .NET semantic view preserves nested
names and inheritance; it does not substitute CLR bodies for native execution.
Native metadata/codegen remain the execution path. Broader bridge replacement work
is tracked independently.

The neoCLR compiled dispatch projection gives retained Object override bodies unique
private names after Object/class dispatch selection, avoiding stale base-slot links
or method hiding. Source metadata remains intact for introspection. Concrete base
ToString implementations remain necessary: native abstract overrides are still a
separate limitation. Eight built-in environment tests pass on macOS ARM64 in each
of interpreter, JIT and native execution, including nested Result/OS patterns,
exhaustive matching, base/Object display, equality and GC lifetime. This is not
mobile/Windows/Linux host qualification. Runtime/library/SDK ownership and exact
hashes are retained in neoCLR's environment-discovery integration evidence.

## Error decorators and native owner interface bounds (2026-10-23 development)

The Error context slice uses ordinary library classes, interfaces and Option values;

The compiler's native declaration planner and metadata SDK previously admitted only

source libraries own the decorators, while runtime StackTraceCapture owns snapshots.
Native default interface bodies and broader structural-union constraint satisfaction
remain gaps. The native specializer validates interface owner bounds before closing
executable shapes; ordinary native project builds now bind the existing opt-in stack
capture service, as JIT already did.

## Compiled worker safepoints (development, 2026-10-23)

neoCLR's opt-in `--native-worker-safepoints` backend mode instruments synchronous
bootstrap callbacks for coordinated GC across worker threads on one heap.
Runtime Contract selection and Raven semantic/emission behavior are unchanged;
the existing temporary CLI encoding of closures, references and bodies is consumed
unchanged. No new language threading semantics or managed API are introduced.

The neoCLR backend owns root snapshots and the private seven-argument worker-root
publication symbol; the native worker coordinator owns suspension, exclusive
allocation/helper execution, shared cursor updates and per-invocation diagnostics.
ABI v4 context layout remains unchanged. Runtime objects must be built with
`NEOCLR_WORKER_GC`. This profile is macOS ARM64 only and rejects type initializers
and unaudited native services. Async Tasks/I/O and arbitrary racing field writes
are not qualified. These are temporary backend admission limits, not Raven rules.
A production native metadata/backend must describe safepoints, participant roots
and transitions directly; CLI bridge conventions are not the final threading ABI.

The matching Raven bundle (1128b98cf) compiles the unchanged language fixture;
optimized/UBSan native tests reach four active participants with live cross-worker
roots through over 24,000 collections. Evidence and reproduction are in neoCLR's
`docs/experiments/native-worker-pool/README.md` and
`compiled-parallel-validation.json`. Default code generation is unchanged.


## Native GC execution-point metadata separation (2026-10-23)

Author direction: use .NET's metadata architecture to guide HTTP runtime efficiency.
The neoCLR native backend now separates its native-GC point payload from the rich
inspection plan: `neoclr-gc-point-v1` carries the ordered `requiredSpillLanes`, while
published slot/lane arrays remain the executable root contract. Diagnostic probes
and inspection retain complete plans. Native-GC frame consumers must recognize the
compact schema rather than expect full type/layout JSON there.

Runtime Contract configuration, Raven CLI metadata/emission and managed semantics
are unchanged. Owner: neoCLR runtime/codegen/src/gc_probe.rs and native root adapter;
Raven codex/neoclr bundle 1128b98cf remains the matching input. This is a temporary
JSON representation, not native CLR GCInfo or the eventual binary metadata ABI.
The native replacement needs versioned maps, image lifetime/unload ownership and
separate diagnostic data. Do not cache validation of arbitrary mutable plan addresses.
The change leaves spill values/order, storage maps, safepoints, fault propagation,
worker exclusion and GC validation intact. Full-plan detail is intentionally absent
only from the native-GC point payload. Validation and measured CPU/object-size
results are recorded in neoCLR benchmarks/http-server/primitive-comparison/allocation-metadata.

Validation: six focused codegen/root-probe tests, forced-GC sanitized HTTP, and
optimized/UBSan compiled shared-worker graph/fault tests pass. Paired one/four-owner
HTTP trials improve throughput about 10% and CPU per response about 9%; application
object size falls 17.3%. These are local observations, not cross-platform capacity
guarantees. Allocation-loop experiments were rejected and are not integrated.

## Generated storage ownership (2026-10-23)

neoCLR's native backend now imports `neoclr_gc_enter_owned_v1` for native-GC
frames. It emits the storage table once in the function prologue. The new entry
validates addresses, widths and flags, then marks storage metadata as exclusively
owned and fixed until frame leave or parked-stack expiry. Live slot values may
change and collection still reads them. Transient descriptors, fault contexts,
plans and ordinary native frames retain their existing checks. Worker safepoint
state preserves the ownership marker; frame leave/reuse clears it.

This is a trusted native caller contract, not memory protection or a process-wide
pointer cache. A native caller that mutates an owned table violates the contract.
Existing `neoclr_gc_enter_v1` objects remain supported on the fully checked path;
newly generated objects require a runtime providing the new symbol. The private
104-byte frame and object headers do not grow. No Runtime Contract setting,
Raven semantic-model behavior, CLI metadata or .NET target behavior changes.
The tested Raven input remains codex/neoclr bundle 1128b98cf; neoCLR's
`runtime/codegen/src/gc_probe.rs` owns native lowering, and `runtime/native/gc`
owns validation/lifetime enforcement. No Raven compiler binary is rebuilt.

Native intent is compiler-owned execution metadata with explicit lifetime. This
slice retains temporary per-invocation descriptor tables and compact JSON; it
does not implement shared binary stack maps or image registration/unloading.
Those remain the eventual native metadata/backend replacement. In particular,
transient tables are rewritten during execution and cannot use this ownership
rule. Malformed entry, mixed checked/owned ancestry, transient mutation, changed
root values, parked collection and frame reuse pass; 11 codegen tests, forced-GC
HTTP and optimized/UBSan shared-worker stress also pass. Evidence and performance
limits are recorded in neoCLR's
`benchmarks/http-server/primitive-comparison/owned-root-storage/README.md`.

immutable-transient metadata contract: the runtime still validates published tables.

The temporary CLI-to-native bridge still uses per-invocation descriptors and compact

## Isolated live-GC scalar-store lowering — 2026-10-24

neoCLR has a private, test-driven Cranelift pass that replaces admitted scalar stores
with the experimental noncollecting `experiment_gc_store` hook. Widths and floating
bit patterns are preserved; rejected writes return the native status before later
stores. Proven stack stores stay direct. The pass must run before return-frame
cleanup, and cannot by itself admit callees, native providers or array publication.
It is not wired into ordinary compilation and adds no public CLI enable switch.

Raven Runtime Contract configuration, source semantics, CLI/NEOX metadata and
ordinary .NET behavior are unchanged; there is no new temporary encoding or lost
metadata. neoCLR owns the pass and matching experimental native host. Broader
integration needs explicit host/image admission and complete writer coverage.
Future native layout/provenance contracts should reduce conservative scalar barriers;
these prototype costs are not permanent language rules. Raven codex/neoclr receives
documentation only and remains separate from main. Qualification and limitations are
recorded in neoCLR `benchmarks/execution/concurrent-store/README.md`.

The isolated lowering also preserves generic stores proven to lie within an explicit
compiler stack slot, including constant-offset addresses, and rejects known invalid
extents before edits. This covers argument copies emitted before GC frame entry and
avoids introducing fallible hooks there. Caller-provided byrefs remain checked;
full frame-entry/return-cleanup integration remains required. No Runtime Contract,
CLI or ordinary compilation behavior changes.

The framed experimental entry now requires completed frame initialization to
dominate every fallible store and return before modifying IR. A shared private
return-cleanup helper preserves production emission and permits exact-path tests.
Mock legacy/state frames and real state-frame JIT/AOT consumers qualify success

## Worker read-phase native contract (2026-10-25)

neoCLR's experimental `--native-worker-safepoints` backend now separates worker
lease classification from GC-point selection. A field/array/indirect write can
lack an allocation point while still requiring exclusive heap access. Mutation
and unreviewed operations now take the exclusive lease; reviewed local operations
and reads may use the shared lease. This is conservative scheduling, not a new
Raven semantic restriction or a complete concurrent-GC admission contract.

The backend emits `neoclr_gc_worker_read_phase_map_v1` and the native adapter marks
its frames distinctly from the legacy allocation-only worker map. Rebuild native
images and hosts together; an old host lacks the new import, and old images must
not be treated as read-phase-qualified merely because the runtime accepts their
legacy callbacks for synchronous execution. Runtime Contract configuration,
Raven semantic model, emitted CLI metadata and temporary bridge encoding are
unchanged. Ownership is in neoCLR native codegen/root publication; eventual native
metadata admission must carry the stronger scheduling capability explicitly.

Validation is recorded in neoCLR `benchmarks/execution/concurrent-read-phases/README.md`:
rebuilt compiled graph/fault/shutdown consumers, copied-root owner controls and
old/new native boundary-tag tests. The forced worker fixture now collects at more
exclusive boundaries; this is safety preparation, not a throughput gain. A future
live epoch must audit all provider paths and finish before any mutation resumes.
No shared-worker concurrent/default or HTTP performance acceptance is implied.

This integration is on neoCLR `main` with documentation on Raven `codex/neoclr`;
no Raven main merge or Raven compiler binary rebuild is implied. Validation uses
the retained Raven-produced sample assembly and newly rebuilt neoCLR native AOT
objects recorded in the linked manifests. JIT worker admission remains open.

payload details are not included in the terminal message.
